subject: Request: latest hosted-API penetration report + encrypted delivery options
messages:
From: Laura Gibbons <laura.gibbons@finservcorp.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: latest hosted-API penetration report + encrypted delivery options

Hi Priya,

We're preparing for an internal risk review and need the most recent penetration test report that covers Redwood's hosted API surface. Specifically:
- Full report (redacted as needed) covering API endpoints, authentication flows, and network boundaries for the hosted offering
- Executive summary + remediation tracker would be ideal
- Delivery must follow FinServ's secure transfer requirements (we prefer S3 presigned links or an encrypted package delivered over a secure portal)

A few clarifying questions: do you redact PoC exploit code and internal hostnames by default? What's your typical turnaround if we need the full redacted report? Are there any paperwork steps (NDA or DPA) we need to complete first?

We can loop in procurement if there are docs to sign.

Thanks,
Laura Gibbons
Sr. Security Manager, FinServ Corp
security@finservcorp.com

[Attachment: none]
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Gibbons <laura.gibbons@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest hosted-API penetration report + encrypted delivery options

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear request. I'm happy to help.

Short answers up front: we redact exploit PoCs and internal-only identifiers by default; we can provide an executive summary within 48 hours and a redacted full report within ~5 business days once we have any required paperwork.

Sharing options we support (pick one):
- Presigned S3 (recommended): server-side encryption (AWS KMS), link expires; we can also provide client-side encrypted ZIP if you prefer additional protection.
- Secure portal link (one-time access): hosted on our secure file portal with audit logs and MFA required.
- Encrypted ZIP delivered over DocuSign/secure email + password exchange (password over phone/2FA).

Redaction policy (summary):
- We remove internal hostnames, internal IPs, and exact PoC exploit code.
- We retain remediation steps, affected component descriptions, CVE identifiers, and severity ratings.
- If you need PoC code for reproduction, we can provide it under a separate controlled disclosure process.

I've attached a provisional executive summary (light redactions) to this reply for your initial review so you can confirm the level of detail you need. If you decide you need the full redacted report, please confirm which transfer option you prefer and whether procurement will execute an NDA or a data sharing addendum.

Next steps:
1) Confirm transfer channel and whether an NDA will be signed.
2) If NDA required, route to procurement (we can accept DocuSign).
3) We'll prepare the full package and provide a secure link + checksum.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan

Thanks, Priya — the executive summary looks good for now.

We do want the full redacted report (remediation items + CVEs are required for our tracker). Procurement will route an NDA; we can sign standard mutual NDA (DocuSign). Our preference is a presigned S3 link with server-side encryption, but we also require a checksum and confirmation of the KMS alias used.

One request on redactions: please keep vulnerability reproductions limited to high-level steps and not include exploit scripts. That's acceptable per your policy.

Please advise expected delivery after we return the signed NDA.

Laura

Hi Laura — looping in details from our side.

Scope confirmation: the report you will receive covers the hosted API surface only (authentication, public endpoints, edge controls, rate limiting, session handling). It does not include customer-managed on-prem deployments.

Planned process once we have the signed NDA:
1) Intake & verification (same-day) — we confirm requester identity and scope.
2) Redaction pass (2 business days) — remove PoCs and internal identifiers; ensure CVE references and remediation steps remain.
3) Packaging & validation (1–2 business days) — create encrypted archive, generate MD5 and SHA256 checksums, and run a final privacy pass.

Delivery mechanics (default/recommended):
- We'll upload the archive to an S3 bucket with server-side encryption (aws:kms) and create a presigned URL set to expire in 14 days. KMS key alias: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:alias/redwood/pentest (we will rotate keys per policy).
- We'll publish checksums in the same email and send an AES-256 ZIP password via a separate channel (phone call or One-Time-Code) — let us know your preference.

Attachments included: Redaction-Checklist-pen-test-2026.pdf (lists items we redact) and a placeholder for the final Redacted-Full-Report-2026-09.zip (will be uploaded after NDA).

Estimated timeline: 5 business days from receipt of signed NDA and confirmation of the delivery channel. If you need an expedited window, we can prioritize but will need a written request from procurement.

Let us know if you need the report mapped to OWASP/CWE or a CSV of findings to import into your tracker — we can include that as an additional artifact.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
